Greptile P1, security, scripts/shell-command-scan.ts:737-740 (PR 84):

"**Reassignment discards final scalar** — When a line contains persistent assignments such as `NPM=ignored; NPM=npm`, this branch deletes `NPM` instead of retaining its final value. A later `\$NPM publish` therefore remains unresolved and is omitted from the audit, allowing an attested sibling to produce a clean result despite the unattested publish. **How this was verified:** The remainder check deletes any same-name scalar, while expansion leaves missing scalars unresolved and publish recognition consequently does not classify \$NPM as npm."

Greptile's 2026-08-28 summary (confidence 1/5) named the same error class from the other direction, and the maintainer asked for it to be re-examined rather than assumed resolved: "it treats pipeline or background assignments as file-wide bindings; either behavior can make static expansion diverge from the shell and conceal missing provenance" — i.e. "pipeline or background assignments are retained as global provenance evidence, while final same-name reassignments are discarded."

CodeRabbit's guidance for the fix: "The reassignment fix should preserve the last persistent, file-scope assignment. It must not promote pipeline, background, or command-prefix assignments into global scalar state."
The scalar scanner deletes a same-line reassignment instead of keeping the shell's final value, and persists pipeline and background bindings
Greptile P1 (security) on PR 84: NPM=ignored; NPM=npm deletes NPM, so a later $NPM publish is omitted from the audit and an attested sibling returns a clean scan over an unattested publish.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
Confirmed both halves by measurement before fixing. NPM=ignored; NPM=npm indexed nothing (delete-branch), so audit([npm publish --provenance, NPM=ignored; NPM=npm, $NPM publish]) returned failures: 0 — a clean gate over an unattested publish. The other direction: NPM=npm | cmd and NPM=npm & cmd were BOTH indexed (bash verifies neither persists: pipeline segments and background jobs run in subshells), so audit([npm publish --provenance, FLAG=--provenance | cat, npm publish $FLAG]) also returned failures: 0 — a false pass.

Fix: replaced the remainder-check/delete branch with lineScalarBinding, a per-line persistence walk. It splits the line into segments at unquoted ; && || & | (quote-, escape-, backtick- and $()-aware; 2>&1 read as one redirection, not a background job), then keeps the LAST binding that runs in the current shell environment: ; && and a & that ends an earlier background job take the later value; | & and a preceding | index nothing; a command prefix keeps the earlier value; || after an assignment-only left side never runs (assignment always succeeds) so the earlier value stands; a reassignment whose execution depends on a real command's exit status, or that sits in a compound command (then/else/{ }), is refused (opaque, name deleted) because either guess can either attest an unflagged publish or hide an unresolved one; NAME+= and non-literal values refuse the same way. Verified against bash for all 14 persistence shapes (A=1; A=2 -> 2, A=1 && A=2 -> 2, A=1 & A=2 -> 2, A=1 || A=2 -> 1, A=1; A=2 | cat -> 1, A=1; A=2 & bg -> 1, A=1; A=2 cmd -> 1, A=1; (A=2) -> 1, export/multi-assignment/2>&1/> file/&> file/append/compound).

value.command: npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a same-line reassignment keeps the final value the shell would end up with"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a redirection on a reassignment is neither a background job nor a pipeline"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a pipeline-component assignment is not global provenance evidence"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a backgrounded assignment is not global provenance evidence"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a command-scoped reassignment leaves the earlier persistent value in place"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a reassignment beside a conditional operator follows the shell's own rule"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a reassignment inside a compound command is refused rather than guessed"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a subshelled or appended reassignment does not carry the earlier value forward"

patch.value: shellScalars now resolves a same-line reassignment the way the shell does: the last binding that runs in the current shell environment wins (; && and a & ending an earlier background job take the later value); pipeline components, background jobs and command prefixes index nothing; || after an assignment-only left side keeps the earlier value; reassignments whose execution depends on a command's exit status or a compound construct, NAME+= appends, and non-literal values are refused with a delete rather than guessed. The walk is quote-, escape-, backtick- and substitution-aware, and reads 2>&1/>file/&>file as redirections rather than separators.

Eight audit-level regressions each fail against the reverted implementation and pass after: a same-line reassignment keeps the final value the shell would end up with; a redirection on a reassignment is neither a background job nor a pipeline; a pipeline-component assignment is not global provenance evidence; a backgrounded assignment is not global provenance evidence; a command-scoped reassignment leaves the earlier persistent value in place; a reassignment beside a conditional operator follows the shell's own rule; a reassignment inside a compound command is refused rather than guessed; a subshelled or appended reassignment does not carry the earlier value forward.

Revert-proof by hand: restoring the old delete-branch reddened exactly the six tests whose assertions the delete-branch answers (84 pass / 6 fail, every pre-existing test green); reverting the conditional rules to uniform last-wins reddened exactly the conditional-operator test (89/1); removing the compound-command refusal reddened exactly the compound test (89/1). Restored: 357/357 across the suite, npm run coverage 100/100/100, npm run check and npm run release:check green. Note: pm test --run cannot execute this repository's suite inside the linked-test sandbox because PM_PATH is reserved there and the repository's own pm-integration tests (coverage-gaps, context-pack, context-handoff - files untouched by this change) collide with it; every linked command was instead executed directly and observed green, including a single-title run of each recorded test.

Replaced the same-name delete branch in shellScalars with lineScalarBinding, a per-line persistence walk verified against bash for all fourteen persistence shapes. Both halves of the finding were measured as live bypasses before the fix (final-value discard: failures 0 over an unattested $NPM publish; pipeline/background indexing: failures 0 over an unflagged $FLAG publish) and both are closed.
